subject: Mapping usage to committed GPUs — Aperture Systems renewal
messages:
From: Jules Martin <jules@aperturesys.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com
Cc: sara.lee@aperturesys.com, procurement@aperturesys.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aperture renewal — usage snapshot + ask

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the hosted trial and the conversations over the last quarter. We're approaching our renewal window and I pulled a quick export of our May usage for the team (attached). High level: peak days drove sustained inference at ~55 GPUs equivalent for short windows, but our 95th percentile sustained is closer to 22 GPUs. Average daily utilization hovered around 14 GPUs.

Questions for Redwood as we plan the renewal:
- How should we map these usage metrics to a committed GPU tranche for Dedicated?
- Can we structure a baseline commit for predictable pricing and keep burst capacity for peak days?
- Any concerns about billing granularity or SLA impacts if we add burst credits rather than raising baseline?

We're also concerned about quality regressions if we switch to a smaller quantized variant under heavy load — we'd prefer an approach that preserves response quality.

Can we get a short plan/estimate from you and schedule a 30-min call next week?

Appreciate it —
Jules Martin
VP, Infrastructure
Aperture Systems

Attachment: gpu-usage-export-may2027.csv (CSV export, columns: date,peak_gpus,median_gpus,p95_gpus,total_tokens)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com>
To: Jules Martin <jules@aperturesys.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal — usage snapshot + ask

Hi Jules — thanks for the export, that helps a lot. Attached is a first-pass tranche matrix that maps sustained percentiles to commit bands and a recommended baseline + burst structure. Summary of our thinking: 

- Convert sustained GPU equivalence to committed slots using the 75th percentile as the safety baseline (in your export that's ~22 GPUs; we recommend a slightly conservative rounding to 25 GPUs for baseline to avoid SLA exceptions).
- Add a burst credit pool sized to cover day-of-week peaks (we modeled a 30% burst pool on top of baseline which covers observed peak windows without forcing a permanent commit).
- Offer an automated fallback policy: when the baseline is saturated, we route to a quantized-compatible variant we validated in staging. That variant preserves ~98% output parity for your top 10 prompt families — we can lock those prompts into a quality-monitoring watchlist.
- Pricing option: a blended rate (baseline discounted commit + pay-for-usage on bursts) or a higher flat commit that absorbs burst. The blended option keeps unit economics predictable while keeping cash commitments lower.

Action items I propose:
1) We book a 30-min review to walk the tranche matrix and assumptions (I suggested Wed Jun 3 at 10am PT).
2) If agreed, we will produce a draft SOW with explicit burst mechanics and rollback/fallback SLAs.

I've attached: proposed-tranche-matrix.xlsx (mapping + pricing scenarios) and a quick checklist for the SOW. Ben and Karthik — looping you for validation on the sizing assumptions and SLA language.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com

1) That 25 GPU baseline you're suggesting — is that sized to avoid model-level throttling for our 99% critical path, or will there still be brief degradations during long-running batch jobs?
2) For the quantized-compatible variant, do you have a short list of the prompt families with the validation results you mentioned? We want to understand risk to our customer-facing SLAs.

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, kimberly_park@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aperture renewal — usage snapshot + ask

Jules / team — quick follow-up after our internal sizing review.

- Baseline recommendation: 25 committed GPUs (matches Stephanie's conservative round-up). This gives room for steady-state and avoids frequent cold fallbacks.
- Burst strategy: 40 GPU-days of burst credits per month (covering observed peak-day spike profiles) with automatic throttling and notification once 80% of burst pool is consumed in a 24-hour window.
- Quality safeguards: we'll include a prompt-watchlist (top 15 prompt families) with daily delta monitoring and an SLA clause that triggers a quality review if regression exceeds agreed thresholds.

Next commercial steps:
- We'll draft SOW v2 with the baseline + burst terms and the pricing schedule (redlines welcome). I've uploaded the draft SOW here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cApertureRenewal (SOW-draft-v2.pdf). Once you sign, we'll provision the Dedicated pool and configure burst credits.

Pricing options attached in the tranche matrix: blended baseline rate (recommended) or flat commit (if procurement prefers single-line budgeting).

If that all looks good we can issue a DocuSign SOW today and target activation on Jun 21 to cover your July peak.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example.com
